messages:
ops-bot: Incident created: KV cache pressure spike impacting streaming paths — automatic pager triggered. severity: P1. Affected: hosted inference (region-us-west).

anita: seeing sudden p95/p99 tail spikes on streaming endpoints. p95 ~ 1.2s -> 3.4s, p99 -> 7.1s. spikes started 02:12 UTC.

jamal: +1 on alerts. graphs?

sara: attaching quick query
```
avg_latency{route="/v1/stream"}[5m]
```
looks like decode time per-token is normal, but prefill latency distribution is bimodal.

leo: logs show frequent KV eviction events and repeated slab reassignments: "evict: slab=3 freed=128KB" every few seconds.

mike: Customer support—two largest enterprise tenants reported degraded streaming; one saw aborted streams and retries.

carla: are dedicated nodes affected or only hosted?

anita: only hosted for now (us-west, pool-3). Dedicated customers on their own pools unaffected.

jamal: hypothesis: prefill vs decode imbalance — prefill load generating many cold-KV reads causing heavy paging and causing tail stalls.

sara: CPU on decode workers fine. GPU queues show short bursts. KV stats:
- slab_utilization=62% -> oscillating
- free_fragments=high
- hot_key_evictions spikes per shard

ops-bot: paging subsystem reported increased page-fault latency: avg 18ms -> 120ms under pressure.

anita: mitigation plan suggestion:
1) pause aggressive prefill for low-priority routes (set rate-limit to 0.1x)
2) bump slab-growth temporarily by +20% on pool-3
3) enable eviction backpressure (reduce prefill concurrency)
4) route high-QPS streaming to fallback lighter model variant

jamal: performing step 1 now: `curl -XPOST https://controlplane/api/pools/pool-3/prefill -d '{"factor":0.1}'` -> 202 accepted

sara: confirm slab growth change requested: `PATCH /internal/kv/pools/pool-3` -> increasing target_slab_bytes  to 80% of node memory.

leo: I'm watching eviction log tail: after prefill cut, evictions per sec dropped 60%.

mike: support: customers on affected tenants report fewer aborted streams now. still seeing intermittent 5-6s completions.

anita: step 2 rolling, but needs node restarts to apply new slab allocation. doing a rolling restart of 3 nodes, will do 1 at a time. ETA ~10m

ops-bot: rolling restart job queued: job-kk72 started.

sara: also toggled decode-prefetch balancing flag (experiment flag `prefill.decode_balance_v2=false`) to reduce prefill concurrency on decode hot paths.

jamal: p95 trending back to ~1.1s after prefill throttle. p99 down to ~3.2s. Still above SLO (p99 target 2s)

carla: we need customer impact summary for postmortem. mike, can you collect a list of affected tenants + start/end times?

mike: yes. pulling from support logs and alert traces. will post CSV link shortly.

leo: suggestion: we should add a TTL-based prefill backoff for hot keys to avoid repeated cold misses. filed a short issue: https://github.com/redwood/infra/issues/5678

anita: proposed next steps for immediate stabilization:
- complete rolling restarts (done ~08m)
- keep prefill throttle at 0.2x for 30m
- monitor eviction rates and p99
- open a follow-up (sre+runtime) to plan slab defrag+hot-key mitigation

jamal: handoff to next oncall @sara in 30m. Leaving runbook notes: `#kv-live-handoff`

sara: acknowledged. will monitor and escalate if p99 > 4s again or eviction rate > baseline*2.

ops-bot: incident status: mitigated (partial). severity downgraded to P2. please update incident doc and attach runbook.

mike: support update posted to customers. customers flagged for follow-up: tenant-47, tenant-99.

carla: thanks team. let's capture action items for postmortem: slab frag root cause, prefill tuning defaults, backpressure heuristics, customer comms.

anita: adding notes to: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-9123

jamal: closing thread and handing off final watch to @sara. if anything spikes again ping me.

sara: will watch dashboard and notify if regressions. :thumbsup:
